title: call, apply, bind, and borrowing a function

videos.script:
Last lesson ended with a method that lost its object. {{lost}} You passed it somewhere, it was called with no dot in front, and this came out undefined.

Today is about taking control of that. {{three}} Every function in JavaScript carries three methods of its own: call, apply and bind. The first two run a function right now, with a this you choose. The third makes a new function with this fixed for good.

That sounds like a niche tool, and for a few years it was everywhere. {{arrows}} Arrow functions and spread replaced most of the old uses, so part of today is learning to read code written before them, and knowing which modern line does the same job.

What has not gone away is borrowing. {{borrow}} A list of elements on a page looks like an array and is not one. A function that belongs to arrays can still be used on it. {{remove}} And one bug with bind still catches people every week: a listener you cannot remove, because the function you pass to remove it is a different function from the one you added.
